In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, while there is a single uPLT distribution, the distribution of objective QoE measures is not a simple function of uPLT.
A single metric cannot capture all of the aspects of user perceived page load.

1) uPLT has a multi-modal distribution; 2) each mode can be approximated by a different objective metric; 3) for a given website, the number of modes is typically small (at most three); 4) the distribution of modes is highly variable across different websites; 5) for a given mode, a single metric is not sufficient to capture its distribution.

The main takeaway from our work is that
, for webpages that contain a large number of objects, a single metric is not sufficient to accurately predict the uPLT, and a combination of multiple metrics is required.
